name: Shade
frame: Roblox studs: Y up, the model on y = 0 facing -Z, HumanoidRootPart at (0, 3, 0)
rig: R6. Every piece carries the body's own surface: the six rig parts are hidden (Transparency 1). The Head carries one mask and nothing else.

emissive.note: One atlas for the five types. The body's five pieces take the type as EmissiveTint and strength as EmissiveStrength. The mask, its own MeshPart with its own SurfaceAppearance, takes mask_tint whatever the type and mask_strength: its paper glows faintly and its cuts are lit in that warm white, so it reads as paper at dusk. Roblox draws (mask x strength x tint + light) x colour map, so the glow mask is written for these two strengths and this colour map: change a strength and every glow scales with it, upload the two maps together. The colour map is a neutral grey under the lit edges and loses its violet where light comes through the cloth. The tints are the sheet's proposal until AR3's gems fix them, and the mask's is tuned in the engine under the game's lighting.

points.name: Crest
points.note: the lit mark on its back

elite.note: An elite wears its own mask twice: the second is the mask's mesh named by `mesh`, with the same surface, mask_tint and mask_strength, at `size` of the first, welded to the Left Arm. Where a copy without ties exists it's that copy (Shade_Mask<Kind>Bare.json: the same triangles, normals and UVs less the strings, the knot and their tails, so the same maps), because a sleeve is too narrow to hide the ties (AR2, section 6). `centre` is where that MeshPart's middle goes and `right`, `up` and `facing` where its own +X, +Y and -Z point, in this recipe's frame at the ordinary Shade's size: all of it scales with the rig. Nothing runs from it to the collar or the first mask. Only the Brawler's is past the content check (docs/asset-requests.md, AR2, sections 5 and 6).
